evidence: src/infrastructure/inMemoryRepositories.ts: InMemoryUserRepository, InMemoryProjectRepository and InMemoryTaskRepository each implement the matching domain repository interface with the same Map-backed save/findById pattern.
src/infrastructure/inMemoryRepositories.ts: InMemoryTaskRepository.findByProject is the only place where TaskFilter's status and assigneeId are applied.
src/infrastructure/app.ts: createApp(service?: TaskManagementService) sends every route through svc.* calls and does not touch the repositories directly. It only constructs them as default wiring.
src/infrastructure/app.ts: the status checks in POST and GET /projects/:projectId/tasks reuse the domain's isTaskStatus, but the error message string is copied in both routes (minor).
src/infrastructure/server.ts: only calls createApp().listen(port), a thin entrypoint.
parsedVerdict.reasoning: The src/infrastructure module has one concern: adapting the domain and application layers to the outside world. Each file has a clear role. app.ts is the HTTP adapter and default composition root, inMemoryRepositories.ts holds the persistence adapters, and server.ts is the process entrypoint. The three repository classes follow one consistent Map-backed pattern and implement the domain's UserRepository, ProjectRepository and TaskRepository interfaces. The task filter rule (status and assignee) lives only in InMemoryTaskRepository.findByProject. app.ts only builds the TaskFilter from query parameters. It does not filter itself. app.ts reaches data only through TaskManagementService, never through the repositories directly, so it does not bypass the module's abstractions. The repositories are only constructed in createApp's default wiring. Status checks in app.ts call the domain's isTaskStatus rather than redefining the allowed statuses. One small issue: the literal message "status must be one of todo, in_progress, done" appears twice in app.ts, in POST /projects/:projectId/tasks and in GET /projects/:projectId/tasks. The rule itself is still single-sourced in isTaskStatus, so I treat this as cosmetic duplication, not a duplicated invariant. The assigneeId type check in the task-creation route may overlap with checks in the service, but the service code is not shown, so I can't confirm a duplication.
